answer: With collateral held in bonded escrows, detected equivocation by k coordinated identities can trigger pairwise-correlated penalties proportional to k(k−1)/2, which scales as O(k²), rather than a flat per-key fine. A swarm exposes more collateral to correlated loss; asymmetric depreciation can further impose an exponential multiplier on capital lost upon detection. Splitting one operator across sybils therefore does not dilute attribution. basalt, saffron, and atlas are labels, not security assumptions.
